## 3. Exploratory Data Analysis

### 3.1 Maize Data Visualization

```{r}
# Maize data distribution - Bar graph with error bars
maize_long <- maize_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Ash, Protein, Fat, Starch, Fiber, Sugar),
               names_to = "Component", values_to = "Value")

# Calculate means and standard errors for maize
maize_summary <- maize_long %>%
  group_by(Sites, Component) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Bar graph for maize proximate composition by site
ggplot(maize_summary, aes(x = Sites, y = Mean, fill = Sites)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SE, ymax = Mean + SE),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  facet_wrap(~Component, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 0),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Maize Proximate Composition by Site",
    x = "Site",
    y = "Composition (Mean ± SE)"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
```

```{r}
# Heatmap of correlations (KEPT ORIGINAL)
maize_cor <- maize_data %>%
  dplyr::select(Ash, Protein, Fat, Starch, Fiber, Sugar) %>%
  cor()

corrplot(maize_cor,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45)
```

### 3.3 Soil Microbial Data Visualization

```{r}
# Combine soil seasons for comparison
soil_all <- soil_season1 %>%
  left_join(soil_season2, by = c("Site", "Replication", "N", "P", "V")) %>%
  mutate(
    Site = as.factor(Site),
    Replication = as.factor(Replication)
  )

# Soil microbial comparison - Bar graph with error bars
soil_long <- soil_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Bacteria_S1, Fungi_S1, Bacteria_S2, Fungi_S2),
               names_to = "Microbe_Season", values_to = "Value") %>%
  separate(Microbe_Season, into = c("Microbe", "Season"), sep = "_")

# Calculate means and standard errors
soil_summary <- soil_long %>%
  group_by(Site, Microbe, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Bar graph for soil microbial populations
ggplot(soil_summary, aes(x = Site, y = Mean, fill = Site)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SE, ymax = Mean + SE),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  facet_grid(Microbe ~ Season, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 0),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "top"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Soil Microbial Populations by Site and Season",
    x = "Site",
    y = "Population (Mean ± SE)"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
```

## 4. Statistical Analysis

### 4.1 Maize Data Analysis

#### 4.1.1 Three-Way ANOVA with Site as Fixed Factor

```{r}
# Function to perform ANOVA for each response variable
analyze_maize <- function(response) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(response, "~ Sites * N * P * V + Error(Replication)"))
  aov_model <- aov(formula, data = maize_data)
  return(summary(aov_model))
}

# Analyze each component
maize_responses <- c("Ash", "Protein", "Fat", "Starch", "Fiber", "Sugar")

maize_anova_results <- lapply(maize_responses, analyze_maize)
names(maize_anova_results) <- maize_responses

# Display results
for (i in 1:length(maize_responses)) {
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("Maize", maize_responses[i], "ANOVA Results\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(maize_anova_results[[i]])
}
```

#### 4.1.2 Mixed Model Approach for Maize

```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)

# Function to fit mixed model
fit_mixed_maize <- function(response) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(response, "~ Sites * N * P * V + (1|Replication)"))
  model <- lmer(formula, data = maize_data)
  return(anova(model))
}

# Fit mixed models
maize_mixed_results <- lapply(maize_responses, fit_mixed_maize)
names(maize_mixed_results) <- maize_responses

# Display results
for (i in 1:length(maize_responses)) {
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("Maize", maize_responses[i], "Mixed Model Results\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(maize_mixed_results[[i]])
}
```

#### 4.1.3 Post-hoc Comparisons for Maize

```{r}
# Function to perform post-hoc comparisons
posthoc_maize <- function(response) {
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste(response, "~ Sites * N * P * V")), data = maize_data)
  
  # Get emmeans
  emm <- emmeans(model, ~ Sites | N | P | V)
  
  # Pairwise comparisons
  pairs <- contrast(emm, "pairwise", adjust = "tukey")
  
  return(list(emmeans = emm, contrasts = pairs))
}

# Example: Post-hoc for Protein
maize_protein_posthoc <- posthoc_maize("Protein")
print(maize_protein_posthoc$contrasts)
```

## 5. Interaction Plots

### 5.1 Maize Interaction Plots

```{r}
# Function to create interaction plots
plot_interactions <- function(data, response, title) {
  # N x P interaction
  p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = N, y = .data[[response]], color = P, group = P)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
    facet_wrap(~Sites) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(paste(title, "- N x P Interaction"))

  # N x V interaction
  p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = N, y = .data[[response]], color = V, group = V)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
    facet_wrap(~Sites) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(paste(title, "- N x V Interaction"))

  # P x V interaction
  p3 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = P, y = .data[[response]], color = V, group = V)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
    facet_wrap(~Sites) +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle(paste(title, "- P x V Interaction"))
  
  return(list(NxP = p1, NxV = p2, PxV = p3))
}

# Maize Protein interactions
maize_protein_plots <- plot_interactions(maize_data, "Protein", "Maize Protein")
print(maize_protein_plots$NxP)
```

```{r}
print(maize_protein_plots$NxV)
```

```{r}
print(maize_protein_plots$PxV)
```

## 6. Correlation Analysis

### 6.1 Maize-Soil Microbial Correlations

```{r}
# Combine maize and soil data
maize_soil <- maize_data %>%
  left_join(soil_season1, by = c("Sites" = "Site", "Replication", "N", "P", "V")) %>%
  left_join(soil_season2, by = c("Sites" = "Site", "Replication", "N", "P", "V"))

# Correlation matrix
maize_soil_cor <- maize_soil %>%
  dplyr::select(Ash, Protein, Fat, Starch, Fiber, Sugar,
                Bacteria_S1, Fungi_S1, Bacteria_S2, Fungi_S2) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

corrplot(maize_soil_cor,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.5,   # smaller numbers (avoids crowding)
         tl.cex = 0.7,       # smaller axis labels
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45,
         title = "Maize - Soil Microbial Correlations",
         mar = c(0, 0, 3, 0))
```
